tool_input.command:
cd <repo>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(hooks): close two push-guard gate bypasses, add fail-safe fallback

Round-1 review found two security-gate bypasses the round-1 fix had
introduced:

1. strip_quotes blanked the interior of any quoted span containing the
   literal word "push" -- including a quoted *subcommand* of a real
   invocation. `git "push" origin main` from a feature branch was
   allowed through outright: the stripper erased "push" before the
   command-position regex ever saw it. Fixed by changing the
   stripper's rule: a quoted interior with no internal whitespace is a
   single shell token (a subcommand, a destination ref, a remote
   name), and quoting it changes nothing about what word it is -- so
   it is unquoted rather than blanked. Only a *multi-word* quoted
   interior (a grep pattern, a sentence) that itself contains the
   phrase is still blanked. The command-position regex is also
   extended to recognize `git`/`push` each optionally wrapped in one
   matching quote character, so a quoted token is classified as an
   invocation whether or not stripping already unquoted it.

2. The stripper's temp file (mktemp) made the whole classification
   gate depend on a writable TMPDIR, and its failure (bad TMPDIR, awk
   missing from PATH) silently produced empty CLASSIFY_TEXT, which the
   command-position check read as "nothing to see here" -- a real
   `git push origin main` was allowed. Fixed two ways: the awk program
   is now fed through process substitution instead of a temp file
   (removing the TMPDIR dependency entirely, closing the mktemp path
   of this bug at the root), and any remaining stripper failure (a
   nonzero exit, or empty output from a non-empty command) now falls
   back to classifying the raw, unstripped COMMAND rather than treating
   failure as "allow" -- the stripper is classification help, never a
   security boundary standing alone, so its absence must only ever
   broaden what the gate looks at, matching the same "a missing
   dependency never degrades to a silent no-op" principle the header
   already states for jq.

Also closed a related gap the probes surfaced in the no-jq command/cwd
extraction path: it never reversed JSON string escaping, so a command
containing an escaped quote or a heredoc's embedded newline arrived at
the classifier as literal backslash sequences rather than the real
shell text jq would hand back -- silently defeating several existing
test cases' coverage under the no-jq PATH without failing them. Added
unescape_json (sed-only, no new tool dependency), reusing jq's decoding
for \", \\, \n, \t, \r, and \/ so both extraction paths agree on what
COMMAND and CWD actually are.

Extended the test suite with the four reproduction cases from review
(quoted-subcommand deny, both quote styles, quoted-subcommand-to-feature-
branch allow, and the pinned-allow quoted-remote-name regression guard)
plus two standalone fail-safe probes (awk absent from PATH, TMPDIR
unwritable) that must still deny a real push to main. All run under
both the jq and no-jq PATHs except the two fail-safe probes, which need
their own environment. 30 cases, 0 failures. Confirmed via fidelity
check: reverting to the round-1 hook reproduces all three bypasses
(exit 0, no deny payload, on a command that must be denied); the fix
denies all three.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <[redacted-email]>
EOF
)" 2>&1
tool_input.description: Commit the round-2 hook fix with test coverage
